sentences.zh: 是的，我参加了那个。

sentences.en: I was at GoSim.
sentences.zh: 我参加了 GoSim。

sentences.en: That was the one in Paris, right?
sentences.zh: 那是巴黎的那场，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you have other conferences coming up?
sentences.zh: 你还有其他会议要参加吗？

sentences.en: Do we have programming language stuff to talk about?
sentences.zh: 我们还有编程语言方面的话题要聊吗？

sentences.en: Programming languages.
sentences.zh: 编程语言。

sentences.en: I don't know that I care about programming languages anymore, Connor.
sentences.zh: Connor，我不知道我是否还关心编程语言。

sentences.en: Honestly.
sentences.zh: 说真的。

sentences.en: I don't know that I care about programming languages.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我是否还关心编程语言。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Maybe that's what the title of this episode will be.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是这期节目的标题了。

sentences.en: Programming languages, do they matter?
sentences.zh: 编程语言，它们还重要吗？

sentences.en: Or like, do programming languages matter anymore?
sentences.zh: 或者说，编程语言现在还重要吗？

sentences.en: Question mark?
sentences.zh: 打个问号？

sentences.en: Go, Bryce.
sentences.zh: Bryce，你来吧。

sentences.en: Talk for 20 minutes and round this episode out.
sentences.zh: 聊个20分钟，给这期节目收个尾。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I'm sure they're still mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的，我相信它们依然很重要。

sentences.en: I do think they still matter and are still important.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为它们依然重要，依然有价值。

sentences.en: But, like, agentic engineering just feels like a higher priority thing for me right now.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，代理工程（agentic engineering）目前似乎是优先级更高的事情。

sentences.en: Because, like, again, my mandate and mission is how do people program parallel platforms?
sentences.zh: 因为，还是那句话，我的使命和任务是研究人们如何对并行平台进行编程。

sentences.en: Specifically, NVIDIA's parallel platform.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是 NVIDIA 的并行平台。

sentences.en: It's sort of my whole career has been around that.
sentences.zh: 我的整个职业生涯基本上都是围绕这个展开的。

sentences.en: And, like, that comes down to, like, how do people get performance out of a platform?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，就是人们如何从平台中获得高性能？

sentences.en: And this is, like, a whole new field of agentic engineering.
sentences.zh: 而代理工程是一个全新的领域。

sentences.en: And, you know, people have been doing programming languages for a long time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们研究编程语言已经很久了。

sentences.en: It's a lot more matured.
sentences.zh: 它已经成熟得多了。

sentences.en: And I feel like there's a lot more to learn and discover here in the world of agentic engineering.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在代理工程的世界里，还有很多东西值得学习和探索。

sentences.en: And, like, how agentic engineering impacts our programming languages, our compilers, our tooling.
sentences.zh: 比如，代理工程如何影响我们的编程语言、编译器和工具链。

sentences.en: Like, that I'm very interested in.
sentences.zh: 这一点我非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: You know, I don't have answers yet for how agentic engineering impacts programming languages.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于代理工程如何影响编程语言，我还没有答案。

sentences.en: I think I'm starting to see how it will impact, you know, tools, compilers, etc.
sentences.zh: 我想我开始看出它将如何影响工具、编译器等等了。

sentences.en: But I don't yet know how it impacts programming languages.
sentences.zh: 但我还不知道它会如何影响编程语言本身。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the one thing I will posit here, and you and I talked about this in the past,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想提出一点，我们过去也讨论过，

sentences.en: is I think there is this question of whether higher level abstractions are more token efficient to reach good performance than lower level abstractions.
sentences.zh: 就是有一个问题：为了达到高性能，更高层次的抽象是否比低层次的抽象更具 Token 效率？

sentences.en: If you're using something like Parrot or Kutile or Triton, can you write good performance code at a significantly lower token cost?
sentences.zh: 如果你使用像 Parrot、Kutile 或 Triton 这样的工具，你能以显著更低的 Token 成本编写出高性能代码吗？

sentences.en: And then can you port that code to a new architecture at a significantly lower token cost?
sentences.zh: 然后，你能以显著更低的 Token 成本将这些代码移植到新架构上吗？

sentences.en: And I think there's a lot of people believe that to be the case.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都认为确实如此。

sentences.en: I have not seen a comprehensive study published evaluating this.
sentences.zh: 但我还没有看到有发表过评估这一点的全面研究。

sentences.en: And I think it'd be great work for someone to do.
sentences.zh: 如果有人能做这项工作就太棒了。

sentences.en: And you could look at it, you could look at things like all these DSLs that popped up, but you could even just evaluate it solely on programming languages.
sentences.zh: 你可以研究一下，比如看看所有这些涌现出来的 DSL（领域特定语言），但你甚至可以仅仅基于编程语言来进行评估。

sentences.en: Like, I think it might be sufficient to look at, like, you know, trying to write, like, some code with, like, C++, C, Python, and Fortran.
sentences.zh: 比如，我觉得看看用 C++、C、Python 和 Fortran 编写一些代码可能就足够了。

sentences.en: And, you know, my guess is that, like, a language like Fortran, which has slightly, like, higher level abstractions,
sentences.zh: 我的猜测是，像 Fortran 这样具有稍微高层一点抽象的语言，

sentences.en: and you don't have to, for stuff like numerical code, you don't have to do as much low level tweaking, but it still gets very good performance.
sentences.zh: 对于数值计算这类代码，你不需要做太多的底层调整，但它依然能获得非常好的性能。

sentences.en: Like, it might show very favorably there.
sentences.zh: 它在那方面的表现可能会非常出色。

sentences.en: So it'd be nice if somebody had, like, an eval suite or a benchmark to do these sorts of evaluations.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人能有一套评估套件或基准测试来做这类评估就太好了。

sentences.en: There probably is something out there like this, I just don't know about it.
sentences.zh: 可能市面上已经有类似的东西了，只是我不知道而已。

sentences.en: But those are the sorts of questions that I think are interesting, is, like, how token efficient are existing languages?
sentences.zh: 但这些是我认为有趣的问题，比如，现有的语言在 Token 使用上有多高效？

sentences.en: Because I don't think we have enough information yet to know how we should evolve programming languages to be more token efficient and agent friendly.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为我们还没有足够的信息来了解我们应该如何改进编程语言，使其更具 Token 效率且对代理更友好。

sentences.en: And I do think the two are linked together.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为这两者是相互关联的。

sentences.en: I think that, like, if you optimize your thing for token efficiency, you are implicitly making it more agent friendly.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果你为了 Token 效率而优化你的东西，你实际上是在隐性地使其变得更对代理友好。

sentences.en: Because what's the most token inefficient thing?
sentences.zh: 因为什么是最浪费 Token 的？

sentences.en: Well, if the agent uses your thing and gets a compilation error or gets a tool failure because it was unclear how to use your thing
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果代理使用你的东西时遇到了编译错误，或者因为不清楚如何使用而导致工具调用失败，

sentences.en: or there were ambiguities or your thing was hard to use, well, that's going to waste a bunch of tokens.
sentences.zh: 或者存在歧义，又或者你的东西很难用，那就会浪费大量的 Token。

sentences.en: So if you just minimize token usage, if that's just your objective function, then you'll make your thing more agent friendly.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你只是最小化 Token 使用量，如果这就是你的目标函数，那么你就会让你的东西变得更对代理友好。

sentences.en: We should just put a loop around that.
sentences.zh: 我们应该直接给它套个循环。

sentences.en: Put a loop around that?
sentences.zh: 给它套个循环？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Just like, like, okay, that's going to be my new answer for anybody who tells me how do I make my thing more agent friendly.
sentences.zh: 就像，好吧，这就是我给任何问我“如何让我的东西对代理更友好”的人的新答案。

sentences.en: I'm just going to say make some eval that uses your thing and then just put an agentic loop around it that's minimizing,
sentences.zh: 我会说，写一个使用你工具的评估程序，然后给它套一个代理循环，目标函数就是最小化……

sentences.en: that subjective function is minimize the number of, you know, tokens to achieve this task.
sentences.zh: 目标函数就是最小化完成任务所需的 Token 数量。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想也是。

sentences.en: You got to isolate, though, to make sure that, like, each time you're launching your, like, prompts,
sentences.zh: 不过你得做好隔离，确保每次启动提示词时，

sentences.en: like, you're going to run into, like, caching and, you know, context bleeding that could, like, affect things, right?
sentences.zh: 你都会遇到缓存和上下文泄露的问题，这可能会影响结果，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think across session you have to worry about caching.
sentences.zh: 我不认为跨会话需要担心缓存问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: Maybe if you don't have to worry about that.
sentences.zh: 也许如果不需要担心那个的话。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure sessions will be isolated, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我很确定会话是隔离的，是的。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure, I'm pretty sure, I mean, I could be wrong about that, but I'm pretty sure the sessions are isolated.
sentences.zh: 我很确定，我很确定，我是说，我可能记错了，但我很确定会话是隔离的。

sentences.en: If not, I'm sure there's a way that you can isolate.
sentences.zh: 如果不是，我相信肯定有办法实现隔离。

sentences.en: We didn't even talk about RuSt.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没聊到 Rust。

sentences.en: So Rust would be the other language to throw in the gauntlet there because Rust has a lot of guardrails on it,
sentences.zh: 所以 Rust 是另一个可以扔进这个挑战里的语言，因为 Rust 有很多护栏，

sentences.en: so it catches a lot of, like, errors, you know, at compile time because it has this correct by construction model.
sentences.zh: 所以它能在编译时捕获很多错误，因为它有这种“构造即正确”的模型。

sentences.en: So, like, the interesting eval would be, like, okay, if you give an agent the same task and ask you to do it in Rust versus C++,
sentences.zh: 所以，有趣的评估会是，如果给代理同样的任务，让它分别用 Rust 和 C++ 来完成，

sentences.en: does it complete it in fewer tokens because in Rust it's just harder to write bad code?
sentences.zh: 它完成任务消耗的 Token 会更少吗？因为在 Rust 中写出烂代码更难？

sentences.en: The answer's probably.
sentences.zh: 答案很可能是肯定的。

sentences.en: Again, I just haven't, like, I haven't seen the study in front of me proving that.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我只是还没看到证明这一点的研究摆在我面前。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You work in research, you should go do that.
sentences.zh: 你是做研究的，你应该去把它做了。

sentences.en: There's already enough people working on Rust, and to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 已经有足够多的人在研究 Rust 了，说实话。

sentences.en: No, no, no, but it's not about RuSt.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，重点不是 Rust。

sentences.en: It's what I'm saying is somebody should evaluate the agent readiness of programming languages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，应该有人去评估编程语言的“代理就绪度”。

sentences.en: I mean, that's adjacent to kind of some of the stuff that I'm working on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这和我正在做的一些工作是相关的。

sentences.en: I'm working on more of, like, the abstraction layer, like, level that you're targeting.
sentences.zh: 我更多是在你所针对的抽象层面上工作。

sentences.en: Like, not dissimilar to when you said Fortran versus, you know, C++ versus Python.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的 Fortran 对比 C++ 对比 Python 那样。

sentences.en: But my more thing is, like, you could even do the same thing within a single language, right?
sentences.zh: 但我的想法是，你甚至可以在单一语言内部做同样的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you know, some high-level thing like Parrot, then Thrust, then Cub, then just Rock, who to C++.
sentences.zh: 比如，一些高层的东西，像 Parrot，然后是 Thrust，然后是 Cub，然后直接用 C++ 的 Rock。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Or just in general, like, yeah, like, if something...
sentences.zh: 或者总的来说，如果某样东西……

sentences.en: And I think that's a really interesting point that maybe I'm conflating abstraction level with programming language here.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常有趣的观点，也许我在这里把抽象级别和编程语言混为一谈了。

sentences.en: I do think that the abstraction level part is the more important question than the specifics of a programming language.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为抽象级别的问题比编程语言的具体细节更重要。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe they are to some degree orthogonal, but what I was really asking about was abstraction level.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许它们在某种程度上是正交的，但我真正想问的是抽象级别。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is in any language, like, I'm not too familiar with Fortran, but, like, even Python, you can, like, you know,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在任何语言中，比如，我对 Fortran 不太熟悉，但即使是 Python，你也可以，你知道，

sentences.en: open up the hood of the car and start doing some crazy stuff with basically, like, C APIs within Python.
sentences.zh: 掀开引擎盖，开始用 Python 里的 C API 做一些疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: And my main thing is, like, which one of these layers, if you're targeting, is going to result in, like, the best outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我的主要观点是，如果你针对这些层中的某一层，哪一层会产生最好的结果？

sentences.en: And I have my own personal theories, but that's...
sentences.zh: 我有我个人的理论，但那是……

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the direction.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那个方向。

sentences.en: It just, what you were saying, though, makes me just think, yeah, like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说的话让我想到，是的，我不知道。

sentences.en: Where do you think, like, five years, ten years from now, where does this all end?
sentences.zh: 你觉得五年、十年后，这一切会走向何方？

sentences.en: Like, I listened to an interview with Boris Churney, and it was, he got asked, you know, what happens when we're post-AGI?
sentences.zh: 我听过 Boris Churney 的一个采访，有人问他，当进入后 AGI 时代会发生什么？

sentences.en: And I won't say his answer, but...
sentences.zh: 我不会说他的答案，但是……

sentences.en: There's always going to be AI doctors.
sentences.zh: 总会有 AI 医生的。

sentences.en: We're always going to need AI doctors.
sentences.zh: 我们永远需要 AI 医生。

sentences.en: That's what you think it is?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, I mean, I think if we think about the state of models today, there's a couple different paradigm shifts that I can imagine happening.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，我是说，如果我们思考当今模型的状态，我可以想象会发生几种不同的范式转移。

sentences.en: One is moving more of thinking and reasoning to happen in the latent space within the model itself.
sentences.zh: 一是将更多的思考和推理过程转移到模型内部的潜在空间（latent space）中进行。

sentences.en: My understanding is that today, most of the reasoning works by model generates an output,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，目前大多数推理的工作方式是模型生成一个输出，

sentences.en: and then takes that back in as an input instead of this all happening within the latent space.
sentences.zh: 然后将其作为输入重新读入，而不是这一切都在潜在空间内完成。

sentences.en: So you hear a lot about, like, the idea of looped transformers and people claiming that maybe mythos is that.
sentences.zh: 所以你经常听到关于循环 Transformer 的想法，人们声称也许 Mythos 就是那样。

sentences.en: But, like, I think that is a thing that is, you know, likely to be a big paradigm shift that'll have big impacts.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这很可能是一个会产生巨大影响的重大范式转移。

sentences.en: It's not as, not something I would expect to impact the agentic engineering part too much.
sentences.zh: 这倒不是我预期会过多影响代理工程的部分。

sentences.en: Although, if the reasoning happens within the latent space, then it's going to be less visible to us than it is today.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果推理发生在潜在空间内，那么它对我们来说就会比现在更不可见。

sentences.en: I mean, it's already probably, the thing that you see that's, that are called, like, thinking traces or reasoning traces are already, like, kind of a lie
sentences.zh: 我是说，其实你现在看到的那些所谓的“思维链”或“推理轨迹”本身就是一种谎言，

sentences.en: because it's, like, it's not really the reasoning trace or it's not really, like, the internal process.
sentences.zh: 因为它并不是真正的推理轨迹，也不是真正的内部过程。

sentences.en: It's just sort of, like, the model, like, generating for you its idea of what the internal process would be.
sentences.zh: 它只是模型为你生成的、它认为内部过程应该是怎样的样子。

sentences.en: Anyways, the other thing is around, like, memory.
sentences.zh: 总之，另一件事是关于记忆的。

sentences.en: So there's all these various systems from memory today, a lot of which kind of boil down to, like, we have some series of markdown files somewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以今天有各种各样的记忆系统，其中很多归根结底就是我们在某处有一些 Markdown 文件。

sentences.en: And I think that there's, like, a lot of room for more first-class memory systems, for memory, longer-term memory of being more of a first-class part of the LLM.
sentences.zh: 我认为还有很大的空间去开发更一流的记忆系统，让长期记忆成为大语言模型中更核心的一部分。

sentences.en: But there's an engineering problem here too, which is how do you, like, manage and build reliable systems that have this, like, self-evolving memory?
sentences.zh: 但这也有一个工程问题，那就是你如何管理和构建具有这种“自我进化记忆”的可靠系统？

sentences.en: So almost all of the eugenic workflows that I'm doing are running on ephemeral VMs.
sentences.zh: 我所做的几乎所有代理工作都是在临时虚拟机上运行的。

sentences.en: So the agent might run for two or three or four days or even a week, but then, like, I'm going to shut down that VM.
sentences.zh: 所以代理可能会运行两三天、四天甚至一周，但之后我会关掉那个虚拟机。

sentences.en: So any, like, information or learning or anything that I take out of that, I'm going to put into skills.
sentences.zh: 所以任何我从中获取的信息、学习到的东西，我都会放入技能中。

sentences.en: I'm going to put into my harness, my tools, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我会放入我的工具库、工具等等中。

sentences.en: I'm not running, like, you know, I come from the HPC world.
sentences.zh: 我不是在运行，你知道，我来自 HPC（高性能计算）世界。

sentences.en: I never run stuff on my laptop.
sentences.zh: 我从不在笔记本电脑上运行东西。

sentences.en: I have, like, a 10-year-old laptop because my laptop's just a thin client.
sentences.zh: 我有一台用了 10 年的笔记本电脑，因为我的笔记本只是一个瘦客户端。

sentences.en: Because at the start of my career, I never ran anything on my laptop anyways.
sentences.zh: 因为在我职业生涯的开始，我反正从不在笔记本上运行任何东西。

sentences.en: My laptop is just an SSH terminal to some node somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我的笔记本只是连接到某个节点的 SSH 终端。

sentences.en: And so I've always sort of had a very different mindset than other developers.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直有一种与众不同的思维方式，不同于其他开发者。

sentences.en: I've never been somebody who's built stuff locally.
sentences.zh: 我从来不是那种在本地构建东西的人。

sentences.en: I'm always doing it somewhere in the cloud.
sentences.zh: 我总是在云端的某个地方做这些事。

sentences.en: And so I'm never running an agent locally on my laptop.
sentences.zh: 所以我从不在本地笔记本上运行代理。

sentences.en: And that means that I've always had to think about, you know, what data needs to be persisted.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我一直不得不考虑哪些数据需要持久化。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people end up, you know, sort of building, like, an agent that has a personality over time, that has memories, longer-term memories, et cetera, that has, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为很多人最终会构建一个随着时间推移具有个性、拥有长期记忆等等的代理，拥有所有这些允许他们进行定制的东西。

sentences.en: all of these things that sort of allow them to customize it.

sentences.en: And, like, you know, I'm sure there's some people that are thinking, blah, blah, blah, terrible for the world.
sentences.zh: 而且，我相信有些人会想，这对世界来说太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's not all terrible, folks.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，并非一切都那么糟糕。

sentences.en: I have become a lawn, what do you call, a lawn enthusiast, you know?
sentences.zh: 我已经成为了一名草坪爱好者，你知道吗？

sentences.en: My Kentucky bluegrass grass front and backyard.
sentences.zh: 我前院和后院的肯塔基蓝草。

sentences.en: How do I know that?
sentences.zh: 我怎么知道的？

sentences.en: Thanks to AI.
sentences.zh: 多亏了AI。

sentences.en: You just send it photos and you say, listen, grade my lawn.
sentences.zh: 你只要发给它照片，然后说，听着，给我的草坪打个分。

sentences.en: I got a D+.
sentences.zh: 我得了D+。

sentences.en: We got lots of Creeping Charlie.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多匍匐查理草。

sentences.en: We got lots of Clover.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多三叶草。

sentences.en: And my wife and I are environmentally conscious, so we're not using any pesticides.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子都有环保意识，所以我们不使用任何杀虫剂。

sentences.en: It's going to be a lot more work.
sentences.zh: 这会需要更多的工作。

sentences.en: We got to use the...
sentences.zh: 我们得用……

sentences.en: This is the Connor equivalent of Bryce's couch story.
sentences.zh: 这就是Bryce沙发故事的Connor版本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好吧，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone, yeah, maybe you're going to be the furniture guy and I'm going to be the lawn care guy.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许你会成为家具达人，而我会成为草坪护理达人。

sentences.en: Because, honestly, I remember my dad.
sentences.zh: 因为老实说，我记得我父亲。

sentences.en: My dad built a table from some wood planks that lived on my grandfather and my grandmother's farm in Terrace, B.C.
sentences.zh: 我父亲用一些木板做了一张桌子，那些木板曾在我祖父母位于不列颠哥伦比亚省Terrace的农场里。

sentences.en: Rest in peace to both of them.
sentences.zh: 愿他们安息。

sentences.en: But they had a wonderful farm and they had these wood planks.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个很棒的农场，有这些木板。

sentences.en: My dad took them.
sentences.zh: 我父亲拿走了它们。

sentences.en: We drove them eight hours to Prince George where I grew up.
sentences.zh: 我们开车八小时把它们运到我长大的Prince George。

sentences.en: He built this beautiful table.
sentences.zh: 他做了一张漂亮的桌子。

sentences.en: And he spent so many weeks slash months.
sentences.zh: 他花了好几周甚至好几个月。

sentences.en: And every single time he would sit down, he would rub his hand on it to look at the quality.
sentences.zh: 每次他坐下来，他都会用手摸摸它，看看质量。

sentences.en: Was it smooth enough?
sentences.zh: 够光滑吗？

sentences.en: Did we need to put another layer of liqueur or whatever they call it on?
sentences.zh: 我们需要再涂一层清漆还是他们叫的那种东西吗？

sentences.en: A lacquer.
sentences.zh: 是漆。

sentences.en: And me and my three sisters would always make fun of him.
sentences.zh: 我和我的三个姐妹总是取笑他。

sentences.en: Because he's always like, we'd sit down to eat.
sentences.zh: 因为他总是那样，我们坐下来吃饭的时候。

sentences.en: And what is he doing?
sentences.zh: 那他在做什么呢？

sentences.en: He's like, ah, you know, this table.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，啊，你知道的，这张桌子。

sentences.en: You know, maybe you got to do some stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许你得做点什么。

sentences.en: I have now become my father.
sentences.zh: 我现在活成了我父亲的样子。

sentences.en: Because every day I basically walk out, especially if it's rained.
sentences.zh: 因为我基本上每天都会走出去看看，尤其是在下过雨之后。

sentences.en: And I am like assessing, you know, oh, did the iron kill enough of the creeping Charlie or the clover or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我会评估一下，你知道，哦，这些铁剂有没有除掉足够多的活血丹、三叶草之类的杂草。

sentences.en: And it is like, it brings me so much joy.
sentences.zh: 这真的带给我极大的快乐。

sentences.en: And also, we have a skunk.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们还有一只臭鼬。

sentences.en: We named him Wilbur.
sentences.zh: 我们给它取名叫威尔伯。

sentences.en: And we had to have a discussion, Shima and I, about whether we were going to get rid of the grubs that are living beneath our grass.
sentences.zh: 我和希玛不得不讨论一下，我们到底要不要除掉草坪底下的那些蛴螬。

sentences.en: Because it is the lunch buffet and dinner buffet for Wilbur the skunk who comes and just digs up these little holes and feeds himself.
sentences.zh: 因为那是臭鼬威尔伯的午餐和晚餐自助餐，它会过来挖出这些小洞，然后填饱肚子。

sentences.en: And Shima said that she was very happy that our lawn was the skunk's lunch and dinner.
sentences.zh: 希玛说她很高兴我们的草坪能成为臭鼬的午餐和晚餐。

sentences.en: So, we're just going to leave, let Wilbur tear up the lawn.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们就随它去吧，让威尔伯把草坪翻个底朝天。

sentences.en: But anyways, I have to go around and like fill in these little holes that Wilbur keeps on digging in our front and back lawn.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，我得四处走走，把威尔伯在我们前后院挖的那些小洞填上。

sentences.en: And like all of this is thanks to AI.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都要归功于人工智能。

sentences.en: I didn't care before.
sentences.zh: 我以前根本不在乎这些。

sentences.en: And then I was like, you know what?
sentences.zh: 然后我就想，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I bet AI could tell me how to like, you know, improve the quality of my lawn.
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌人工智能能告诉我该怎么做，你知道的，改善我的草坪质量。

sentences.en: And sure enough, it's...
sentences.zh: 果然，它……

sentences.zh: 我要给你买把椅子，这样你就可以坐在那儿冲孩子们大喊：离我的草坪远点。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: If the kids want to play on my lawn, they can play on my lawn.
sentences.zh: 如果孩子们想在我的草坪上玩，他们尽管玩就是了。

sentences.en: Anyways, the point is, it's not all bad, folks.
sentences.zh: 总之，重点是，伙计们，这并不全是坏事。

sentences.en: If you, you know, give it a chance, it'll make you fall in love with your lawn as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你，你知道，给它一个机会，它也会让你爱上你的草坪。
